text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall-ryan — multiple nodes reporting Xid errors + ECC correctable spikes in us-west-2-gpu-pool. Autoscaler observed increased evictions and several containers restarted. Initial anomaly started ~5198765400 UTC. Logs attached below.

oncall-ryan: Acknowledged. I'm looking at alert group now. Which nodes? any customer-facing impact?

sre-jen: Nodes: gpu-n-12, gpu-n-17, gpu-n-21. Observed repeated nv-hostengine resets and dmesg shows correctable ECC logs. Telemetry: Xid 43 followed by kernel reset on 3 different hosts in ~6m.

eng-runtime-maya: Seeing a pattern where kvcache OOMs spike after driver reset; containers hit OOMKilled in the same pods running long-running inference. Stack traces show eviction during KV cache warm-up.

infra-oliver: I'm seeing driver module reloading on gpu-n-17. Running `ssh gpu-n-17 sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver | tail -n 80` shows repeated: 
```
Mar 12 09:03:21 gpu-n-17 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 43, PID=0e4a, GPU was stopped.
Mar 12 09:03:21 gpu-n-17 kernel: NVRM: Xid 43: General Protection Fault.
Mar 12 09:03:22 gpu-n-17 kernel: EDAC MC0: Corrected error, CPU 2.
```

support-luis: Support note — we've started getting a handful of error reports from customers with higher LQ traffic in us-west-2. Latency spikes ~2-3s and some requests 5xx. Triage shows retries succeeded after a few seconds for most. No confirmed data loss.

product-maria: Ping — any customers at risk of SLA breach? We should prepare a bridge if there's sustained impact.

incident-bot: Added incident severity: P2. Current aggregate error rate for hosted inference endpoints in region: +4.8% above baseline.

oncall-ryan: Ok. Immediate plan: 1) Isolate affected nodes (cordon + drain if necessary). 2) Fall back routing for critical customers to other regions. 3) If hardware errors continue, open HW ticket. 4) Start customer comms draft. Who can take node cordon?

infra-oliver: I'm cordoning gpu-n-17 and gpu-n-21 now: `kubectl cordon gpu-n-17` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. I'll drain them to reduce noisy resets.

eng-runtime-maya: Suggest also reducing kvcache size for ongoing rollouts to avoid OOM spikes during node swap. Quick change: set env REDWOOD_KVCACHE_MAX_BYTES=2147483648 on the inference daemonset for the pool to trim memory footprint while we recover. Can do a patch and rollout.

oncall-ryan: Good. @eng-runtime-maya go ahead with patch. @infra-oliver hold reboots until after we've drained to avoid double resets.

infra-oliver: Drains in progress. gpu-n-17: pods gracefully terminating. gpu-n-21: pod eviction rate high, some pods restart on warm nodes — tracking.

eng-runtime-maya: Patch applied as a rolling update to the pool with zero-downtime strategy: `kubectl set env ds/inference REDWOOD_KVCACHE_MAX_BYTES=2147483648 -n redwood-serving`. Monitoring logs.

sre-jen: Telemetry shows Xid occurrences dropped after cordon and env change on the warm hosts. However gpu-n-12 still has recurrent ECC correctables. I'll run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` remotely: 
```
GPU 0
    ECC errors
        Volatile
            Single-bit ECC errors: 12
            Double-bit ECC errors: 0
```

support-luis: Customer impact update: three customers reported 5xx bursts, one (acme-ml) had end-user facing retries. I've flagged them as priority, prepping a proactive note. No data exfiltration or corruption reported; only transient failures.

product-maria: Draft for comms: short note explaining transient instability in us-west-2 GPU pool, mitigation in progress, expected restoration in <2h. Will liaise with legal if needed.

hardware-ops: For gpu-n-12 we recommend a hardware-level ECC scan and possibly a DIMM reseat — plan to RMA if correctables persist after reboot. Need approval to schedule maintenance window.

oncall-ryan: Approve RMA prep if we still see >10 single-bit ECCs/hour after a clean reboot. For now, continue draining and routing. @support-luis include customers in priority list for warm-failover.

eng-runtime-maya: Observed a container crash stack snippet where process exited due to mmap failure: 
```
E valgrind: failed to allocate 0x1b774000 bytes: Cannot allocate memory
runtime: out of memory: Kill process 12034 (server) score 987
```
Adjusting kvcache cut memory spikes immediately removed similar OOM traces in new pods.

infra-oliver: After draining, I performed a cold reboot on gpu-n-12 and ran ECC memtest. Post-reboot, single-bit ECC counts reset to 0 but we still saw a stray Xid 43 at 5198765490 on gpu-n-12. Opening a COS ticket for vendor driver investigation.

hardware-ops: Noted. We'll queue hardware inspection but mark low-priority until we confirm recurring hardware faults.

support-luis: Customer comms sent to acme-ml & beta-ai: brief apology + mitigation steps + contact for escalation. Both acknowledged; acme-ml requested an incident postmortem.

noncall-ryan: Handoff prep — current state: pooled impact reduced to <1% error rate, drained two noisy hosts, kvcache reduced, rolling update in flight, vendor ticket opened. Next oncall should monitor for reappearance of Xid 43 or ECC single-bit increases.

product-maria: Noted. Please include estimated root cause hypothesis in postmortem: driver/hardware interaction under KV cache memory pressure leading to kernel recoverable Xid resets.

oncall-sam: Taking over for next shift. I'll be available to coordinate with hardware-ops and support for customer follow-ups. ETA to take full responsibility 08:00Z.

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P3 at 5198765590 — error rate returned near baseline. Oncall handoff to oncall-sam scheduled.

oncall-ryan: Thanks team. Quick action points for handoff: 1) Watch ECC counters (EDAC) on drained nodes for 30m post-reboot. 2) Keep driver ticket open and push vendor logs: `dmesg + journalctl` snippets and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv`. 3) Postmortem owner: @product-maria to coordinate, @eng-runtime-maya to provide runtime memory traces.

support-luis: I'll continue customer follow-ups and prepare SLA impact report if acme-ml escalates.

eng-runtime-maya: I'll open a temporary regression alert to catch kvcache growth regressions during rollouts.

oncall-sam: Copy — will watch for any resurgence. If Xid > 5 occurrences in 1h, I'll escalate to hw-ops for immediate RMA.

oncall-ryan: Signing out. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Thread closed to new automated alerts for this incident at 5198765600.
